November 10, 2026

House Republicans block vote on Hegseth impeachment articles

tags: politics, legal, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy, @groundnews

The House voted 211-204 on November 10 to refer Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, halting a floor vote on the charges. The articles center on Operation Epic Fury in Iran, which Massie says has run 256 days without congressional authorization, and also cite operations in Yemen and Venezuela. Eleven Democrats did not vote; their absence was enough to change the outcome, and critics circulated their names alongside figures on career AIPAC-linked donations. At a Pentagon news conference, Hegseth called the effort a farce, said every operation was a lawful order from the commander-in-chief that he would carry out again, and Democrats have signaled they may revive impeachment after taking control of Congress in January.

Account details missile strikes on Iranian school at start of 2026 war

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A detailed account describes the opening hours of the US-Israeli offensive into southern Iran on February 28, 2026, when three Tomahawk cruise missiles fired from US Navy warships struck an elementary school between 10:23 and 10:45 a.m. local time. Because the operation began on a Saturday morning, between 170 and 264 students were reported present despite an attempted evacuation, and survivors sheltering in a prayer room were hit by the second and third missiles. Reported death tolls put the civilian toll at at least 156, including roughly 120 schoolchildren and 26 teachers. The strikes form the factual basis of the impeachment case brought against the defense secretary.

Whistleblowers say Interior Department is destroying Trump project records

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

CNN has reported that whistleblowers told members of Congress that officials inside the Department of the Interior have begun destroying documents related to President Trump's construction projects ahead of expected Democratic investigations. The projects named include the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, the East Potomac Park Golf Course, a triumphal arch and a planned ballroom. Rep. Jared Huffman is expected to demand that the department preserve all related records. Federal records carry statutory preservation requirements and prescribed procedures for disposal.

USDA rule would cut 6.3 million people from SNAP

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

A proposed rule from the US Department of Agriculture would end automatic SNAP eligibility for households receiving cash aid under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program, according to Reuters. TANF eligibility generally runs from 130% to 200% of the federal poverty level depending on the state, while SNAP's threshold is 130%, so households above that line would lose benefits. The change would remove about 18% of SNAP recipients, roughly 6.3 million people, on top of about 5.5 million already cut.

Supreme Court lets border barrier construction resume at Big Bend

tags: legal, immigration, climate
sources: @groundnews

The US Supreme Court granted an emergency request from the Trump administration on Monday to resume border barrier construction in West Texas, lifting a federal judge's order that had blocked work in the Big Bend region while litigation proceeds. The Center for Biological Diversity and other plaintiffs are challenging Homeland Security waivers that allow the project to bypass environmental and historic preservation laws. US District Judge Kathleen Cardone had ruled that Congress gave the department no clear authority to issue those waivers. The administration plans to install 17 miles of vehicle barriers in segments within Big Bend National Park.

Senate advances Mike Lee permitting bill that fast-tracks data center power

tags: politics, climate, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

The Senate voted 73-25 on Monday to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, S.5653, co-written by Sen. Mike Lee, with support from some Democrats. The bill funds new transmission lines and requires data centers to pay their own way on the grid, but also fast-tracks the gas plants, pipelines and nuclear reactors that power them, bars judges from halting construction on projects found to break the law, and makes approved permits difficult for a future administration to reverse. Critics are asking for five changes, including restoring judicial injunctions, dropping indefinite permits, restoring Tribal consultation and state water protections, removing the nuclear section pending a public hearing, and guaranteeing clean energy access to new transmission. A final vote is expected soon.

Anthropic sets terms for IPO that could value it near $1.3 trillion

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews

Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, pricing on November 18 and trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT from November 19, in an offering that could raise as much as $64.35 billion. The company had targeted a $2 trillion valuation but investors have grown wary that rising interest rates will make borrowing more expensive for AI firms financing infrastructure. About 20% of shares are reserved for retail investors, and seven technology companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google have agreed to buy $26 billion in a separate private placement. Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026 and a $104 billion net loss driven largely by accounting adjustments on convertible debt and derivative liabilities.

Nvidia chief tied to woman US intelligence calls a Chinese spy

tags: tech, politics, surveillance
sources: @carolinegleich

Claims that Utah residents opposing a Box Elder County data center were funded by China were made on NBC by Kevin O'Leary, who later acknowledged he had no evidence; the interview was pulled. The New York Times has since reported that Nvidia's chief executive, who spent the past year successfully lobbying the White House to allow sales of advanced chips to China, has acknowledged a romantic relationship with a businesswoman US intelligence identifies as an agent of the Chinese government. Her company was suspected by federal agents of smuggling Nvidia chips into China, and that investigation stalled after an email from an Nvidia lawyer.

Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader, replacing Mike Johnson

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Jim Jordan has been elected leader of the House Republican caucus, defeating Steve Scalise. Mike Johnson is out of the post. Jordan will serve as House minority leader in the next Congress.

Democrats on track for largest House majority of the century

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

One week after election day, Democrats hold at least 258 seats in the House of Representatives, with counting continuing and the total possibly exceeding 260. That would give the party its largest House majority of this century.

Pennsylvania Democrats plan 100-day agenda after winning trifecta

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

With Democrats holding the governor's office and both chambers of the Pennsylvania legislature, Gov. Josh Shapiro has said the party will move to raise the state minimum wage to $15 an hour, codify abortion rights in the state constitution, fund mass transit statewide and expand housing construction. The goal is to complete the agenda within the first hundred days after the legislature is sworn in. Republican legislators had previously blocked much of it, including the minimum wage increase.

Sanders open to impeaching RFK Jr

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Sen. Bernie Sanders, who chairs the Senate health committee, said he would be open to moving forward with an impeachment of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. He was responding to incoming South Carolina Senator Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, who has called for Kennedy's removal. Kennedy, Todd Blanche and other cabinet secretaries have been named as possible impeachment targets once Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Corporations sue to block Michigan campaign finance measure

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Michigan's Proposal 2, which would force disclosure when corporations fund political advertising and limit corporate money in state politics, passed by a wide margin. Within hours of the result, large corporations filed suit seeking to stop the measure from taking effect. The litigation would delay or prevent implementation of the voter-approved disclosure rules.

California voters reject billionaire wealth tax

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews

California's Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of billionaire residents, is on course to fail 54% to 46% with 76% of ballots counted, Decision Desk HQ projected. It would have been the first such tax in the United States, with most proceeds going to health care and the remainder to food aid and education. The measure split Democrats, with the state party backing it and Gov. Gavin Newsom opposed. California billionaires, including Silicon Valley executives, gave more than $333 million to Building a Better California to defeat it.

Global carbon emissions fall as Iran war disrupts oil markets

tags: climate, markets, war
sources: @groundnews

Worldwide carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels fell 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2 billion metric tons, according to the Global Carbon Project. Researchers attributed the decline to oil market disruption from the war in Iran, which cut petroleum shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and pushed fuel prices up. Emissions from oil fell about 2% while emissions from coal rose 0.6%.

Hegseth press conference restricted to friendly outlets as reporters are warned

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

At a Pentagon news conference, a security agent for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned reporters they could be physically removed from the briefing room if they did not remain professional and maintain decorum, according to reporter Tara Copp. Hegseth took questions only from right-wing outlets. Journalists present described the warning as unprecedented treatment of the Pentagon press corps.

Incoming Ohio Democrat says leadership threatened him over Israel and Jeffries

tags: politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

Rep.-elect Don Leonard of Ohio's 15th district said that at freshman orientation senior House Democrats told him his position on supporting Hakeem Jeffries was not negotiable. He said he was warned that pressing his two priorities, a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United and ending US support for the war in Iran and for Israel, would make his life in Washington difficult and cost him his seat in two years. The account has been cited as evidence of pressure on new members to fall in line with party leadership and its donors.

Justice Department political appointees move toward the exits

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Current and former officials say Justice Department political appointees are seeking to leave after the midterms, according to Bloomberg Law. Appointees reportedly fear that association with an agenda voters rejected will damage their careers, and Stephen Miller's elevation to chief of staff has prompted outreach to private sector contacts. The departures follow four Senate-confirmed exits in a single week.

Britain to spend £90 million countering Russian undersea threats

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

Britain will spend 90 million pounds on drones, sensors and artificial intelligence to counter Russian threats to undersea infrastructure in the North Atlantic, according to Reuters. The Atlantic Net system is the first phase of the Royal Navy's Atlantic Bastion programme to protect undersea cables and energy networks. The government says the work will support almost 200 jobs.

El-Sayed launches leadership PAC days after winning Michigan Senate seat

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed formed Habibi PAC within days of winning a Senate seat, according to Federal Election Commission filings. The leadership committee will raise money for allies and operate separately from his Senate campaign, and takes its name from an Arabic term of affection he used in his victory speech while addressing Vice President JD Vance. El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers by a wide margin in a state expected to be a battleground in 2028.

New York Times publishes Trump's 2021 letter to Biden

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times has obtained the handwritten letter Donald Trump left in the Oval Office for Joe Biden in January 2021. In it Trump called working in the office a blessing, urged Biden to take stock of the presidents who came before him, and wrote that Biden would change history because of how much he loves the American people. The letter was written days after the January 6 attack on the Capitol and while Trump was publicly attacking Biden.
